tip: A question clause can be the whole subject: 'var hon bor' = where she lives.
Exclamations use 'vad' + adjective + subject + verb: 'vad vacker hon var' = how beautiful she was.
'Liten' is irregular: you say 'en liten stad', but the plural is 'små', which looks nothing like 'liten'.
After a linker like 'så att', 'inte' comes before the verb: 'så att vi inte missar'. Main clauses put the verb before 'inte'.
'Fick', the past of 'få', often means 'had to': 'vi fick beställa pizza' = we had to order pizza.
The pattern 'i' + weekday + '-s' means 'last': 'i fredags' = last Friday.
Swedish 'i' marks a duration you spent: 'pratade i en timme' = talked for an hour.
Some verbs form the past by changing the vowel: 'dricka' becomes 'drack' = drank.
'Få reda på' means to find out: 'fick reda på vad som hänt'.
Unlike English 'that', 'att' is normally kept in reported speech: 'viskade att han hade en hemlighet'.
Verb forms used as adjectives take '-a' when definite: 'det sjunkna skeppet' = the sunken ship.
When 'snart' (soon) opens the sentence, the verb moves before the subject: 'snart kommer sommaren', not 'snart sommaren kommer'.
'Tack' means both please and thank you: 'nej tack' declines an offer, 'ja tack' accepts it.
Swedish splits 'know': 'vet' (from 'veta') is knowing a fact, as in 'jag vet inte'. Knowing a person uses 'känner'.
The '-s' ending can mean each other: 'hörs', from 'höra' (hear), is a set phrase for we will be in touch.
To tell time say 'klockan är' plus the number: 'klockan är tre', literally the clock is three.
Language names stay lowercase in Swedish: 'svenska', not 'Svenska', even elsewhere in a sentence.
In a main clause 'inte' normally follows the verb: 'det kan inte stämma'.
Tens from 30 up end in '-tio', from 'tio' (ten): 'sjuttio' (70), 'åttio' (80), 'nittio' (90).
'Sju' (seven) starts with the 'sj'-sound, often called the hardest sound in Swedish, made deep in the throat.
Teens 13 to 19 end in '-ton', with the digit sometimes tweaked: 'tretton' (13), 'fjorton' (14), 'femton' (15).
'Sjutton' (17) doubles as a mild exclamation like darn in 'sjutton också', besides just meaning seventeen.
For minutes before the hour use 'i' (to): 'tio i tolv' means ten to twelve, pointing ahead to the next hour.
For minutes after the hour use 'över' (past): 'fem över åtta' means five past eight.
A reported question keeps the subject before the verb: 'var vi bodde', not 'var bodde vi'.
State age with 'är' plus 'år gammal': 'jag är tjugofem år gammal'. In everyday speech 'gammal' is often dropped.
Definite adjective phrases double the marking: 'den stora bilen' has 'den', the '-a' on 'stora', and the '-en' ending on 'bilen'.
After 'är', adjectives match the noun. 'Soppan' is an 'en'-word, so 'varm' and 'god' take no ending.
'Dem' is the object form of 'de' (they): 'vi förde dem till hotellet'.
Swedish has no '-ing' form: 'flyttar' covers both we move and we are moving. Present tense does the job.
